name: Kimham
title: Barzillai's Son and David's Companion
summary: Kimham was the son of Barzillai the Gileadite, a wealthy man who had supported King David during his flight from Absalom. When Barzillai declined David's invitation to come to Jerusalem due to his advanced age, he sent his son Kimham in his place. David took care of Kimham and treated him with great kindness.

keyEvents.title: Barzillai Supports David During the Flight
keyEvents.description: Barzillai from Gilead was among those who brought supplies to David and his people as they fled from Absalom. This act of kindness laid the foundation for David's gratitude toward Barzillai's family.

keyEvents.title: David Invites Barzillai to Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: After Absalom's rebellion was crushed, David wanted to reward Barzillai by inviting him to come to Jerusalem and be supported there. Barzillai declined due to his advanced age.

keyEvents.title: Kimham Sent with David in His Father's Place
keyEvents.description: Barzillai asked David to take Kimham instead of himself. David agreed and promised to do for Kimham whatever Barzillai desired.

keyEvents.title: David's Final Wish Regarding Barzillai's Sons
keyEvents.description: On his deathbed, David instructed Solomon to show kindness to the sons of Barzillai and let them eat at the king's table, in gratitude for how Barzillai had helped him while he fled from Absalom.

keyEvents.title: Kimham's lodging near Bethlehem
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah mentions a lodging (Gerut Kimham) near Bethlehem that bore Kimham's name, suggesting that David had given Kimham land holdings in this area.
